design_notes.detection: The suite asks the HOST, independently of tools/linux_trial_sandbox.sh and the trial adapter, by running exactly one fixed command, `unshare --user --map-root-user true`: no shell, no repository file, no trial runner, no fixture content, stdin=/dev/null, a 20 s timeout. `true` is the system utility, so no unsafe or untrusted code runs during detection. The probe uses the same PATH lookup of `unshare` as the sandbox script and as the acceptance tests' own capability probe, so the suite and AT1/AT2/AT4 always agree about the host. It runs lazily, once per process, only when an isolation-dependent test is about to run (a `-k` selection of other tests never probes: S12). ANY failure to prove isolation (unshare absent, non-zero exit, timeout, OSError) means 'unavailable'; the probe can only ever REMOVE tests from the run (report them UNSUPPORTED), it never grants anything. Soundness: the sandbox script's namespace flags are a superset of the probe's (--user --map-root-user plus --net --ipc --uts --pid --fork --mount-proc), so a host that refuses the probe necessarily refuses the sandbox -- every host reported unavailable already failed these tests before this feature. Residual case: a host that passes the probe but cannot create the remaining namespaces still runs the tests, the unchanged fail-closed sandbox refuses, and the tests FAIL loudly (never skip, never pass): proven by S10.
design_notes.outcome_vocabulary: UNSUPPORTED is the explicit, reported outcome. It is carried as a unittest skip whose reason starts with the pinned prefix 'UNSUPPORTED: user-namespace isolation unavailable' (plus a parenthesised host detail), so it appears on the test's own result line (the description's wording), and it is counted by prefix, so ordinary skips (the pre-existing jsonschema-ImportError skipTests) are never mistaken for it. CONFORMANCE: FULL / CONFORMANCE: NOT FULL is the run-level verdict. The exact lines are pinned in design_notes.output_contract.lines. CONFORMANCE speaks only about the isolation-dependent tests and run success; the jsonschema-ImportError skips keep their existing behaviour (see non_goals).

output_contract.stream: All CONFORMANCE and note lines are written to stderr, after unittest's own summary, so they follow unittest's `Ran N tests` / `OK (skipped=N)` / `FAILED (...)` summary in the merged output the acceptance tests read.
output_contract.when_printed: Exactly one CONFORMANCE line per run. FULL iff the run was successful (no failure, error or unexpected success) AND no isolation-dependent test was reported UNSUPPORTED. NOT FULL otherwise. The required note is printed only when at least one UNSUPPORTED outcome occurred and the flag was NOT given; the allow note only when at least one UNSUPPORTED outcome occurred and the flag WAS given. Nothing containing the words UNSUPPORTED or skipped is ever printed on a run with zero UNSUPPORTED outcomes (AT1's capable branch forbids both words anywhere in the output).
output_contract.result_line: Each of the five tests keeps unittest's single verbose result line `<test_name> (<module>.<Class>.<test_name>) ... skipped 'UNSUPPORTED: user-namespace isolation unavailable (<detail>)'`. AT1/AT2 match `^<test_name>\b.*\bUNSUPPORTED\b` line-anchored, so the line must begin with the test name on ONE line: unittest moves the output after a newline when a test has a docstring, so the five tests must not gain a docstring and the decorator must preserve __name__ and __doc__ (functools.wraps).

mode_switch.default: Required-conformance mode is the DEFAULT and has no switch: the documented 'required gate' command `python3 tools/test_convergent_review.py` never passes on a host that cannot prove isolation.
mode_switch.relaxation: The ONLY relaxation is the explicit command-line flag --allow-unsupported-isolation (local development only; CI never passes it). There is deliberately no environment variable, no config file and no CI auto-detection that could relax the mode implicitly.
mode_switch.exit_status: 0 iff the unittest run was successful AND (no isolation-dependent test was reported UNSUPPORTED OR the flag was given). 1 in every other case: any failure, error or unexpected success is 1 whether or not the flag is given; UNSUPPORTED without the flag is 1. No new exit-code vocabulary: 1 is also what the suite returned before for these hosts.
mode_switch.flag_scope: The flag converts only the UNSUPPORTED outcome. It never masks any other failure: AT3 proves it on this host and S13 proves it host-independently (UNSUPPORTED and FAIL lines both present, exit non-zero).
mode_switch.polarity: Opposite of NIP-0003's sketched --require-isolation opt-in; this feature sets the framework precedent (required by default). The divergence is already recorded for the NIP's pre-acceptance revision in docs/planning/backlog_reconciliation.md (D-14); this contract does not edit that file.

design_notes.no_unsandboxed_fallback: Never, by construction and by proof. (1) tools/linux_trial_sandbox.sh, tools/isolated_trial_adapter.py and tools/evaluate_convergent_review_prompt.py are not modified (AT5 at 02b02c6, S07 and S14 at <A>). (2) The unavailable branch is a skip BEFORE the test body: no trial command is started, no alternative adapter is selected, and the suite never passes --isolation-adapter or any other adapter override. (3) The module gains exactly one subprocess call -- the fixed-argv probe (S14). (4) S09's shim log shows that on an isolation-less host the only unshare invocation in the entire 54-test run is the single probe, and every trial path in the suite goes through unshare (the sandbox script's exec), so no trial ran. design_notes.available_isolation_branch: When the probe succeeds the decorator calls the original, untouched test body, which drives the real sandbox. The Generator cannot observe the real branch on this host. Evidence that the gating genuinely runs the discriminating tests rather than skipping them is simulation of the gating logic, NOT capable-host evidence: S10 (probe passes, sandbox refused -> exactly five FAIL lines, no skips, five sandbox invocations); S17 (the same under --allow-unsupported-isolation: the flag does not mask them); S18 (capable shim: the five tests execute and pass, the bare CONFORMANCE: FULL is printed, and ordinary jsonschema skips are not mistaken for UNSUPPORTED); S08 (bodies identical to base, so the discriminating assertions are intact). What AT4's mutation proves on a capable host (amendment A1): removing BOTH isolation halves -- the unshare namespace line of tools/linux_trial_sandbox.sh and the Landlock restrict-self call of tools/isolated_trial_adapter.py -- turns test_linux_sandbox_blocks_cross_trial_files_and_network into a FAIL line with 'AssertionError: 40 != 0' (the cross-trial secret was read), discharged in CI by feature 104 AT7/AT8. KNOWN LIMIT (NDEBT-046): removing the namespaces alone is detected by no test (Landlock still enforces the file leg and the network leg passes on any OSError), so AT4 proves that removing isolation is detected through the filesystem leg only; making the sandbox tests discriminate the namespaces is outside 103's scope. On a RESTRICTED host (this one) AT4's mutation is inert: the probe skips the sandbox tests before they run, so AT4's restricted branch passes with or without the mutation and proves only that the UNSUPPORTED outcome appears.
design_notes.host_security_settings: Never altered. The suite only runs the probe command and, in S16 only, READS /proc/sys/kernel/apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns. pinned_texts.readme_paragraph: On a host that cannot prove user-namespace isolation (for example one whose kernel refuses `unshare --user --map-root-user true`, as with `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns = 1`), the five sandbox-dependent tests are not run. Each is reported on its own result line as `UNSUPPORTED` (an explicit skip whose reason begins `UNSUPPORTED: user-namespace isolation unavailable`), the run prints `CONFORMANCE: NOT FULL`, and the command exits non-zero: the required gate never passes on a host that cannot prove isolation. `--allow-unsupported-isolation` is for local development only and CI never passes it; it turns that same outcome into exit 0 while still printing every `UNSUPPORTED` line and `CONFORMANCE: NOT FULL`, and it never masks any other failure. On an isolation-capable host the sandbox tests execute and the run prints `CONFORMANCE: FULL`. `linux_trial_sandbox.sh` and `isolated_trial_adapter.py` are not relaxed by this mode and still fail closed; the suite never runs a trial outside the sandbox.
